incident.title: [DEMO C047] Gmail attachment sends fail before reaching Google
incident.description: Attachment sends fail with validation errors because the client passes a signed download URL as the attachment argument, while plain-text sends work.

tasks.question: Scope and coordinate the evidence-led incident investigation.

Using canonical executor/request validation logs with null filters first, what records exist for the affected tenant and time window that show: total failed Gmail send attempts vs successful plain-text sends, exact validation error messages, whether any outbound Google API request was emitted, request latency distribution, retry counts, and whether impact is limited to attachment-bearing executions or broader across tenants/services?

What exact workflow/tool input shape changed or differed between failing attachment sends and successful plain-text sends during 2026-11-12T09:50:00Z–10:15:00Z, and were there any nearby changes in client argument construction, toolkit/version pinning, schema validation, or attachment handling configuration that could explain a signed download URL being passed where a supported attachment object/reference is expected?

Do the canonical records support a pre-provider validation failure mechanism specific to attachment argument shape—distinguishing it from Google/provider failure, credential/auth issues, permissions, payload limits, or an internal regression—by showing failing requests rejected before egress while a discriminating control (same tenant/tool with plain-text send) succeeds?
Challenge the diagnosis, evidence grounding and verification gaps.
Write the evidence-backed internal report and proposed next steps.

objections: The candidate marks ev_370b5ecdbb78 as contradicting evidence, but that query returned no records; an empty partial reproduce search is not counter-evidence and should not be used that way.

The version-control finding is slightly overstated from its citation: the cited record proves an unrelated support-dashboard deployment existed, but the absence of tool-executor deployments comes from a separate empty scoped query and is weaker than a positive record.

notes: Observed failing Gmail send in cedar used attachment_argument_type=string_signed_url while validator expected uploaded_file_object; it was rejected locally with validation_error=attachment_object_required and provider_called=false, so the request did not reach Google. A controlled sandbox comparison passed when the only changed input shape was attachment_argument_type=uploaded_file_object, after which provider_called=true. Citations: ev_1a9957dc86e7/gmail-shape-047:logs:0, ev_74f478a0842b/gmail-shape-047:reproduce:0, ev_74f478a0842b/gmail-shape-047:reproduce:1

Impact appears tenant-specific in observed data: cedar had 738 requests with 420 failures, 420 blocked operations, queue_depth 132, p95 latency 1760 ms, while comparison tenant maple had 604 requests, 0 failures, queue_depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms; maple also had an unrelated successful read on the same provider availability. Citations: ev_603d36f62204/gmail-shape-047:metrics:0, ev_603d36f62204/gmail-shape-047:metrics:1, ev_3562733ffb41/gmail-shape-047:logs:1

Nearby change evidence is limited and does not show a tool-executor rollout in the incident window: the only deployment found was an unrelated support-dashboard release at 10:05Z, and the scoped tool-executor deployment query returned no records. Citations: ev_4b15d5f650ae/gmail-shape-047:deployments:0

Important gap: no canonical log in the supplied records shows a successful plain-text Gmail send or the exact client-side argument construction/version/schema/config that produced the signed URL. Empty scoped dependency/plain-text reproduce queries cannot prove no such change existed, only that it was not surfaced by those exact queries. Citations: ev_a68b18a4b624 has no records, ev_5d18375ed7dc has no records, ev_370b5ecdbb78 has no records

Canonical executor logs in the incident window show one observed cedar Gmail failure record at 2026-11-12T10:05:00Z: request req-47 returned 400 with attachment_argument_type=string_signed_url, expected_attachment_type=uploaded_file_object, validation_error=attachment_object_required, and provider_called=false, indicating no Google-bound request was emitted for that logged failure (ev_1a9957dc86e7/gmail-shape-047:logs:0).

Affected-tenant aggregate metrics for cedar at 10:05 show 738 requests, 420 failures, 420 business operations blocked, queue_depth 132, and p95 latency 1760 ms; comparison tenant maple shows 604 requests, 0 failures, queue_depth 0, p95 latency 160 ms, suggesting impact is observed in cedar rather than broad platform-wide in the supplied records (ev_2545920a7512/gmail-shape-047:metrics:0; ev_603d36f62204/gmail-shape-047:metrics:1).

Cross-tenant canonical logs provide limited counter-evidence against a provider-wide Gmail outage: maple has a 200 success with same_provider_available=true and unrelated_read_succeeds=true during the same window, but this is an unrelated read, not a plain-text Gmail send, so the requested count of successful plain-text sends is not established from supplied canonical records (ev_42cd001d24f1/gmail-shape-047:logs:1).

Important gaps: supplied canonical records do not enumerate total failed Gmail attachment-send attempts versus successful plain-text sends, do not provide per-request latency distribution beyond tenant p95, and do not show retry-count records; empty retry/plain searches are not proof of absence, so those fields remain unverified from current evidence (ev_79a4f1faa0bb; ev_370b5ecdbb78).

events.question: Do the canonical records support a pre-provider validation failure mechanism specific to attachment argument shape—distinguishing it from Google/provider failure, credential/auth issues, permissions, payload limits, or an internal regression—by showing failing requests rejected before egress while a discriminating control (same tenant/tool with plain-text send) succeeds?

hypothesis.description: Observed Gmail send failures are most consistently explained by local validation rejecting an attachment argument shaped as a signed URL string instead of the required uploaded file object, preventing egress to Google.
assumptions: Conclusion is scoped to the observed failed execution(s) and cedar impact in supplied records, not all Gmail sends everywhere.
Controlled sandbox reproduction verifies the attachment-shape variable, but supplied canonical production records do not include a successful plain-text Gmail send for the same tenant/window.
Empty exact-match searches do not prove absence of other changes or controls.

findings.statement: Canonical executor log for cedar shows a Gmail request rejected with status 400, validation_error=attachment_object_required, attachment_argument_type=string_signed_url, expected_attachment_type=uploaded_file_object, and provider_called=false, directly supporting a pre-provider validation failure.
The observed failed request did not call the provider, which distinguishes this mechanism from Google/provider failure, provider payload limits, or provider auth errors on that execution path.

In controlled sandbox observations, the original request shape with string_signed_url failed before provider call, while the corrected request using uploaded_file_object succeeded and did call the provider; the changed variable was the Gmail attachment configuration.

Observed impact is concentrated in cedar: 420 failures and 420 blocked operations out of 738 requests, with queue_depth 132 and p95 latency 1760 ms, while comparison tenant maple shows 0 failures out of 604 requests, queue_depth 0, and p95 latency 160 ms.

A comparison tenant had a 200 response with same_provider_available=true and unrelated_read_succeeds=true during the window, which is counter-evidence to a broad Gmail/provider outage, though it is not a plain-text send control.

No tool-executor deployment was found in the incident window; the only nearby deployment record is an unrelated support-dashboard release, weakening an internal executor regression explanation based solely on timing.

actions: Pass the supported uploaded file object for Gmail attachments rather than a signed download URL string, and validate serialized attachment arguments before send.
Collect a canonical production control showing the same tenant/tool succeeds for non-attachment or correctly shaped attachment sends in the same window.
Capture the exact client-side argument construction/schema path that emitted string_signed_url so recurrence can be prevented.

Canonical telemetry tying the bad attachment shape to the originating client/config/schema path is not supplied.
